precepts.text: Therefore shall ye lay up these my words in your heart and in your soul, and bind them for a sign upon your hand, that they may be as frontlets between your eyes. In ancient times Israel would wear the laws wrapped around their arms and on their foreheads. That is the seal Solomon meant.
precepts.point: The Song of Solomon is a metaphor: the whole book represents the Lord's relationship with his chosen people Israel. Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm. The heart is the mind. What is the seal? The law, the words of God.

note.label: 250 Years of Celebration 400 Years of Sweat Equity (Pt 2)

precepts.why:
The Song of Solomon is a metaphor: the whole book represents the Lord's relationship with his chosen people, Israel. So what did Solomon mean, in his righteousness, when he said “Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm”? The heart is the mind. What is set as a seal upon our mind and upon our arm? Is it the six-point hexagram? Heck no. Here is what he was referring to.

“Therefore shall ye lay up these my words in your heart and in your soul”. These my words are the laws of God, laid up in your heart, meaning your mind. “and bind them for a sign upon your hand, that they may be as frontlets between your eyes.” In ancient times Israel would write the laws on leather and wrap them around their arms. Those were the frontlets, and the frontlets between your eyes are on your forehead.

So go back to the Song: “Set me as a seal upon thine heart”, that's the mind; “as a seal upon thine arm”. The seal is the law, the laws of God, the words of God, bound on the arm and laid up in the mind. People who will not be proven wrong search for scriptures that use the word shield or seal and try to make them say it is the Star of David, forcing a square peg into a circle. That is a complete lie; the seal is the law.

precepts.text: God has another land his eyes are upon for a different reason: behold, the eyes of the Lord are upon the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from off the face of the earth. America is a sinful kingdom. Saving that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob: Jacob is the father of the twelve tribes. I will sift the house of Israel among all nations, because we were scattered into all nations; the sifting is a teaching process. All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword, which say, The evil shall not overtake nor prevent us: that's what America, aka Egypt, has convinced you to believe, that nothing can happen to you here because Donald Trump talks tough about the strongest military and the Strait of Hormuz.
precepts.point: A land which the Lord thy God careth for: the eyes of the Lord thy God are always upon it.

note.label: Are You A Strong Independent Woman?

precepts.why:
Deuteronomy 11:12 says the land God gives is “A land which the Lord thy God careth for: the eyes of the Lord thy God are always upon it”. God has his eyes upon a specific place for us. But there is another land his eyes are upon for a different reason.

“Behold, the eyes of the Lord God are upon the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from off the face of the earth”. America is a sinful kingdom, and God is looking at America to destroy it. “saving that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob, saith the Lord.” Jacob is the father of the twelve tribes of Israel.

“For, lo, I will command, and I will sift the house of Israel among all nations, like as corn is sifted in a sieve, yet shall not the least grain fall upon the earth.” We were scattered into all nations in slavery and captivity, so he will sift us out of every place we went. The sifting is a teaching process: our people have been trained after the ways of their colonizers, their oppressors and enslavers, and now they must be trained in the word of God to establish the house of Israel.

“All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword, which say, The evil shall not overtake nor prevent us.” Those are our people who are rebellious to what God has to say and want to do things their own way. That is what America, aka Egypt, has convinced you to believe: nothing can happen to you here. You hear Donald Trump saying we have the strongest military, no one can stop us, open the Strait of Hormuz or I will blow you back to kingdom come. Stop believing you cannot be touched because this man talks tough and proud. America's kingdom is temporary; the strength that lasts comes from keeping God's commandments.

precepts.text: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations: because we were scattered into all nations, we have to be taught in all nations. That's why you see the bishop giving the order: look historically where our people were slaves, and train them how to behave for God, to establish the kingdom, because they've been trained after the ways of their colonizers.
precepts.point: A land which the Lord thy God careth for: the eyes of the Lord thy God are always upon it.

note.label: Are You A Strong Independent Woman?

precepts.why:
Amos 9:9 says, “I will sift the house of Israel among all nations”. Christians read Matthew 28:19 and think it means make everyone disciples: “Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost”.

This is what it means: because we were scattered into all nations, we have to be taught in all nations. It is the same sifting Amos speaks of. Christ himself, when he started his ministry, told the twelve, “Go not into the way of the Gentiles”, but “go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” Teaching all nations is going into all the nations where the lost sheep were scattered.

That is why the bishop gives the order: look historically at where our people were slaves, and go there and train them how to behave for God, to establish the kingdom. They have been trained after the ways of their colonizers, so we must train them in the word of God. The brothers who travel find the hardest thing is telling oppressed people that Jesus Christ is not a white man, because that white Jesus, made up in the Renaissance, is how the colonizers modified their behavior. But the charge stands: tell our people, you are not black, not Hispanic, not West Indian, not African; you are the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

precepts.text: As the days of heaven upon the earth.
precepts.point: Those who believe enter into rest, and those who did not believe were kept out.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“That your days may be multiplied, and the days of your children, in the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers to give them, as the days of heaven upon the earth.” What does Moses mean? When you go into the land and keep the commandments, it will be as the days of heaven upon the earth.

Moses saw Adam's kingdom. That is why he could say that going into the land and keeping the laws would be as the kingdom of heaven upon the earth. The kingdom of heaven was once on the earth, when Adam was ruling.

So the promise of Hebrews 4:1, “a promise being left us of entering into his rest”, is the same promise: heaven's days upon the earth again. “There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.” Those to whom the word was first preached “entered not in because of unbelief”, “For we which have believed do enter into rest”. The one who has entered into his rest has “ceased from his own works”: the works are our labouring in this earth to bring forth the kingdom of heaven.

precepts.text: Unto thy seed have I given this land, from the river of Egypt unto the great river Euphrates.
precepts.point: Jubilee began only when Israel entered the land, and the land's borders are in the Middle East.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
Before Genesis, Deuteronomy 11 was read from verse 21, the word the Lord gave Israel in advance of entering the land: “That your days may be multiplied, and the days of your children, in the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers to give them, as the days of heaven upon the earth.” For us, heaven has always been upon the earth. If Israel would diligently keep the commandments, “Then will the Lord drive out all these nations from before you, and ye shall possess greater nations and mightier than yourselves.” To possess means to own. Then: “Every place whereon the soles of your feet shall tread shall be yours”. Every place your feet touch is your land; that is heaven on earth.

With a map on the screen, verse 24 lays out the borders. “From the wilderness” is the wilderness of Egypt, on the other side of the Nile. “And Lebanon” sits at the top of the map, and Lebanon was ours. “from the river, the river Euphrates” runs through Syria, just above Lebanon. “even unto the uttermost sea” is the Mediterranean on the left. So the land ran from the wilderness of Egypt all the way up to the Euphrates, taking in Syria and everything down from it.

Genesis 15:18 goes with Deuteronomy 11:21-24. “In the same day the Lord made a covenant with Abram, saying, Unto thy seed have I given this land, from the river of Egypt unto the great river, the river Euphrates”. The river of Egypt is the Nile. The same land God promised Abraham is the land Israel took. We were fighting from the time of Joshua to get all of it, and we fully had it under David and Solomon.

This matters for Jubilee. Jubilee did not start until Israel got into the land: count seven times seven years, forty-nine, and the fiftieth year is the jubilee, when the land rests and every piece of land goes back to the original owner of that heritage, that tribe. So the land has borders, and they are in the Middle East. The doctrines going around that the Congo, or Kenya, is the real Israel cannot stand. What are y'all talking about? It gives you the land layout right here. The hell is this?

From there Isaiah 14 shows the land coming back: “For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land”. He is not having mercy on everybody, only Jacob. We may be at the bottom of society, but he will yet choose Israel, and it is God who sets us in the land, not the League of Nations or the United Nations. “And the people shall take them, and bring them to their place”: every nation goes back to the land God first gave it, and “the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids”. The laws of Leviticus 25 cannot be in effect now while we are the slaves in a foreign land, but when we return to the land they go back into full effect.

precepts.text: Hearken diligently unto his commandments, and he gives the rain of your land in his due season and grass in thy fields for thy cattle, that thou mayest eat and be full.
precepts.point: From the questions: a land flowing with milk and honey is not a magical land of milk. It means a plenteous, fertile land of great landscape, valleys, grass, and fields, with cattle and goats grazing for the milk, and flowers and plants in abundance for the bees to make the honey; a land blessed as the days of heaven upon the earth.

note.label: Exodus 33: My Presence Shall Go with Thee

precepts.why:
“Unto a land flowing with milk and honey”: not a magical land of milk. It means a plenteous, fertile land, and Deuteronomy describes it: “if ye shall hearken diligently unto my commandments which I command you this day, to love the Lord your God, and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul, That I will give you the rain of your land in his due season, the first rain and the latter rain, that thou mayest gather in thy corn, and thy wine, and thine oil. And I will send grass in thy fields for thy cattle, that thou mayest eat and be full.”

Grass in the fields for the cattle and goats grazing, that is the milk; valleys, fields, flowers and plants in abundance for the bees, that is the honey. A land of great landscape, watered in due season.

precepts.text: That your days may be multiplied in the land which the LORD sware unto your fathers, as the days of heaven upon the earth.
precepts.point: From the questions: a land flowing with milk and honey is not a magical land of milk. It means a plenteous, fertile land of great landscape, valleys, grass, and fields, with cattle and goats grazing for the milk, and flowers and plants in abundance for the bees to make the honey; a land blessed as the days of heaven upon the earth.

note.label: Exodus 33: My Presence Shall Go with Thee

precepts.why:
“That your days may be multiplied, and the days of your children, in the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers to give them, as the days of heaven upon the earth.”

This is the land the Lord sware unto Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, “Unto thy seed will I give it”. A land flowing with milk and honey is a land blessed as the days of heaven upon the earth: plenteous and fertile, with cattle and goats grazing for the milk and flowers and plants in abundance for the bees to make the honey.

precepts.text: The Egyptians pursued into the midst of the sea; the Lord took off their chariot wheels, the sea returned to his strength, and there remained not so much as one of them.
precepts.point: This is part of the history Moses was recounting: remember what the Lord did for your fathers.

note.label: Deuteronomy 11: Remember His Acts, Keep His Commandments

precepts.why:
Here is the history Moses recounts, to the generation whose own eyes saw it. “And the Egyptians pursued, and went in after them to the midst of the sea, even all Pharaoh’s horses, his chariots, and his horsemen.” In the morning watch the Lord looked unto the host of the Egyptians through the pillar of fire and of the cloud and troubled them, “And took off their chariot wheels, that they drave them heavily: so that the Egyptians said, Let us flee from the face of Israel; for the Lord fighteth for them against the Egyptians.”

Then the Lord told Moses to stretch out his hand over the sea, “and the sea returned to his strength when the morning appeared; and the Egyptians fled against it; and the Lord overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea. And the waters returned, and covered the chariots, and the horsemen, and all the host of Pharaoh that came into the sea after them; there remained not so much as one of them.”

That is “what he did unto the army of Egypt, unto their horses, and to their chariots; how he made the water of the Red sea to overflow them as they pursued after you”. Remember what the Lord did for your fathers: he took the wheels off their chariots, brought the sea back on them, and destroyed them unto this day.

precepts.text: Two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly gathered against Moses and Aaron, saying all the congregation are holy, wherefore lift ye up yourselves.
precepts.point: Moses set the proof before them: if these men die the common death of all men, the Lord hath not sent me; but if the Lord make a new thing and the earth open her mouth and swallow them, then ye shall understand that these men have provoked the Lord.

note.label: Deuteronomy 11: Remember His Acts, Keep His Commandments

precepts.why:
What the Lord did unto Dathan and Abiram is the rebellion of Korah in Numbers 16. “And they rose up before Moses, with certain of the children of Israel, two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly, famous in the congregation, men of renown”. Not nobodies: princes, famous, men of renown. And they told Moses and Aaron, “Ye take too much upon you, seeing all the congregation are holy, every one of them, and the Lord is among them: wherefore then lift ye up yourselves above the congregation of the Lord?”

The same spirits are back on the earth today. They come into the congregation, and after a season they rise up thinking themselves wiser than the leadership, the bishop and the deacons: ye take too much upon you, all the congregation is holy. Nothing new under the sun. Moses set Israel to remember what happened to Dathan and Abiram so that spirit would be known for what it is.

precepts.text: Hereby ye shall know the Lord hath sent me: if the Lord make a new thing and the earth open her mouth and swallow them, these men have provoked the Lord.
precepts.point: Moses set the proof before them: if these men die the common death of all men, the Lord hath not sent me; but if the Lord make a new thing and the earth open her mouth and swallow them, then ye shall understand that these men have provoked the Lord.

note.label: Deuteronomy 11: Remember His Acts, Keep His Commandments

precepts.why:
Moses set the proof before them: “Hereby ye shall know that the Lord hath sent me to do all these works; for I have not done them of mine own mind. If these men die the common death of all men, or if they be visited after the visitation of all men; then the Lord hath not sent me.” He put it in the Lord's hands to show who he had sent.

“But if the Lord make a new thing, and the earth open her mouth, and swallow them up, with all that appertain unto them, and they go down quick into the pit; then ye shall understand that these men have provoked the Lord.” Whether Moses and Aaron took too much upon them was going to be answered by the Lord, not by the princes. That is what Moses tells Israel to remember: “how the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up”, in the midst of all Israel, and their eyes saw it.

precepts.text: The earth opened her mouth and swallowed them up, and they went down alive into the pit, and perished from among the congregation.
precepts.point: Moses set the proof before them: if these men die the common death of all men, the Lord hath not sent me; but if the Lord make a new thing and the earth open her mouth and swallow them, then ye shall understand that these men have provoked the Lord.

note.label: Deuteronomy 11: Remember His Acts, Keep His Commandments

precepts.why:
“And the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up, and their houses, and all the men that appertained unto Korah, and all their goods. They, and all that appertained to them, went down alive into the pit, and the earth closed upon them: and they perished from among the congregation.” The new thing Moses spoke of came to pass exactly as he said it, so all Israel understood that those men had provoked the Lord.

That is the history behind Moses' words: “how the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up, and their households, and their tents, and all the substance that was in their possession, in the midst of all Israel”. Their households and all their substance went down with them. “But your eyes have seen all the great acts of the Lord which he did.” The generation Moses is speaking to saw it, and the same spirits that rise up against the bishop and the deacons today should remember how the Lord answered that rebellion.

precepts.text: The Lord shall open his good treasure, the heaven to give the rain unto thy land in his season; thou shalt lend unto many nations and shalt not borrow.
precepts.point: This is the blessing side that Deuteronomy 28 spells out: when Israel kept the commandments, the Lord gave rain in due season in Israel's own land. Chapter 28 comes up in the reading in a few days; these are the basic precepts for it.

note.label: Deuteronomy 11: Remember His Acts, Keep His Commandments

precepts.why:
This is the blessing side that Deuteronomy 28 spells out. “The Lord shall open unto thee his good treasure, the heaven to give the rain unto thy land in his season, and to bless all the work of thine hand”. That is the same rain as here: “the rain of your land in his due season, the first rain and the latter rain, that thou mayest gather in thy corn, and thy wine, and thine oil.” When Israel hearkened diligently to the commandments, loving the Lord and serving him with all their heart and with all their soul, the Lord gave rain in due season in Israel's own land.

The blessing goes further than rain: “the Lord shall make thee plenteous in goods, in the fruit of thy body, and in the fruit of thy cattle, and in the fruit of thy ground, in the land which the Lord sware unto thy fathers to give thee”, and “thou shalt lend unto many nations, and thou shalt not borrow.” Corn, wine, oil, and grass in the fields for the cattle, that thou mayest eat and be full: it all hangs on hearkening to the commandments. Chapter 28 comes up in the reading in a few days; these are the basic precepts for it.

precepts.text: Thy heaven shall be brass and the earth iron; the Lord shall make the rain of thy land powder and dust, until thou be destroyed.
precepts.point: The things written aforetime were written for our learning: Jeremiah shows this curse landing in Israel's history, the ground chapt because there was no rain, and the confession that our backslidings are many.

note.label: Deuteronomy 11: Remember His Acts, Keep His Commandments

precepts.why:
The second part is the curse. If the heart is deceived and Israel turns aside to serve other gods, “the Lord’s wrath be kindled against you, and he shut up the heaven, that there be no rain, and that the land yield not her fruit”. Deuteronomy 28 spells out what a shut heaven is: “And thy heaven that is over thy head shall be brass, and the earth that is under thee shall be iron. The Lord shall make the rain of thy land powder and dust: from heaven shall it come down upon thee, until thou be destroyed.”

A heaven of brass gives no rain, and an earth of iron yields no fruit. No rain means drought: the crops cannot grow, and with no grass the animals have nothing to feed on, so the cattle go lean and there is no meat to eat. What comes down from heaven instead of rain is powder and dust, until thou be destroyed; that is how ye “perish quickly from off the good land which the Lord giveth you.”

precepts.text: Whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning; the history shows where the shut heaven happened.
precepts.point: The things written aforetime were written for our learning: Jeremiah shows this curse landing in Israel's history, the ground chapt because there was no rain, and the confession that our backslidings are many.

note.label: Deuteronomy 11: Remember His Acts, Keep His Commandments

precepts.why:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” The curse of the shut heaven was not written as a warning that never landed. It was written aforetime, and the history shows where it happened: Jeremiah records the ground chapt because there was no rain, and the confession that our backslidings are many.

So we go to the history for our learning. Moses said take heed that your heart be not deceived, lest the Lord shut up the heaven; Israel's own history shows the heaven shut. Reading what was written aforetime, we learn what turning aside to other gods brings, and through the scriptures we have hope.

precepts.text: The ground is chapt, for there was no rain; the hind forsook her calf and the wild asses' eyes did fail because there was no grass, for our backslidings are many, we have sinned against thee.
precepts.point: The things written aforetime were written for our learning: Jeremiah shows this curse landing in Israel's history, the ground chapt because there was no rain, and the confession that our backslidings are many.

note.label: Deuteronomy 11: Remember His Acts, Keep His Commandments

precepts.why:
Here is the shut heaven landing in Israel's history. “Because the ground is chapt, for there was no rain in the earth, the plowmen were ashamed, they covered their heads.” Exactly what Moses warned: the Lord shut up the heaven, there was no rain, and the land did not yield her fruit; the plowmen had nothing to show.

“Yea, the hind also calved in the field, and forsook it, because there was no grass. And the wild asses did stand in the high places, they snuffed up the wind like dragons; their eyes did fail, because there was no grass.” With no grass the animals have nothing to feed on: the hind forsook her own calf, and the eyes of the wild asses failed. The crops cannot grow, the cattle go lean, and there is no meat to eat.

And the reason is confessed: “O Lord, though our iniquities testify against us, do thou it for thy name’s sake: for our backslidings are many; we have sinned against thee.” The heart was deceived, Israel turned aside, and the drought came just as Deuteronomy 11 says. These things were written for our learning.

precepts.text: The blessings of obedience that run through Deuteronomy 28:1-14: hearken diligently and all these blessings shall come on thee and overtake thee.
precepts.point: The blessing is what Deuteronomy 28:1-14 describes; the curse is what came upon Israel, running through Deuteronomy 28 to verse 68.

note.label: Deuteronomy 11: Remember His Acts, Keep His Commandments

precepts.why:
Moses sets before Israel “a blessing and a curse”. The blessing is what Deuteronomy 28:1-14 describes, and it opens this way: “And it shall come to pass, if thou shalt hearken diligently unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe and to do all his commandments which I command thee this day, that the Lord thy God will set thee on high above all nations of the earth: And all these blessings shall come on thee, and overtake thee, if thou shalt hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God.”

That is the blessing “if ye obey the commandments of the Lord your God”: set on high above all nations of the earth, with blessings that come on thee and overtake thee. Hearken diligently and observe to do all his commandments; the blessings run from verse 1 through verse 14 on that one condition.

precepts.text: The end of the curses that came upon Israel for not obeying: brought into Egypt again with ships and sold unto their enemies.
precepts.point: The blessing is what Deuteronomy 28:1-14 describes; the curse is what came upon Israel, running through Deuteronomy 28 to verse 68.

note.label: Deuteronomy 11: Remember His Acts, Keep His Commandments

precepts.why:
The curse is what came upon Israel, running through Deuteronomy 28 to verse 68, and this is its end: “And the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships, by the way whereof I spake unto thee, Thou shalt see it no more again: and there ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you.”

That is the curse “if ye will not obey the commandments of the Lord your God, but turn aside out of the way which I command you this day, to go after other gods”. Israel did turn aside, and the curses came all the way to the end: brought into Egypt again with ships and sold unto their enemies for bondmen and bondwomen. Blessing and curse were both set before Israel this day; the curse is the one our history shows.

precepts.text: Hearken diligently and he gives the rain in due season, that thou mayest gather thy corn, thy wine, and thine oil; the increase that is tithed is the increase he gives.
precepts.point: Today Israel is disconnected from that fear because the oppressor nourishes us; the food comes from the grocery store. That understanding must be brought back to our people, and that is why the laws are read four chapters a day, from Genesis all the way to Revelation, to gain the understanding that we are the Israelites.

note.label: Deuteronomy 14: A Peculiar People and the Clean Foods

precepts.why:
The tithe is of “thy corn, of thy wine, and of thine oil”, the increase of thy seed year by year. Chapter 11 shows where that increase comes from: “if ye shall hearken diligently unto my commandments which I command you this day, to love the Lord your God, and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul, That I will give you the rain of your land in his due season, the first rain and the latter rain, that thou mayest gather in thy corn, and thy wine, and thine oil.”

The corn, wine, and oil tithed here are the same corn, wine, and oil promised in chapter 11 for hearkening to the commandments; this all goes together. The increase that is tithed is the increase he gives.

If Israel did not keep the commandments, he would shut up the heaven, there would be no rain, the land would be chapt, and famine would teach the fear of the Lord. That is the tithe eaten before him “that thou mayest learn to fear the Lord thy God always.”

Today Israel is disconnected from that fear because the oppressor nourishes us; the food comes from the grocery store. That understanding must be brought back to our people, and that is why the laws are read four chapters a day, from Genesis all the way to Revelation, to gain the understanding that we are the Israelites.

precepts.text: Days as the days of heaven upon the earth; if ye diligently keep the commandments, every place whereon the soles of your feet shall tread shall be yours, no man shall be able to stand before you, and the Lord shall lay the fear and dread of you upon all the land, the very promise repeated to Joshua.
precepts.point: This is the same word the Lord foretold to Moses that Joshua now fulfills. The promised land was meant to be as the days of heaven upon the earth, and the condition was diligently keeping all the commandments, to love the Lord, to walk in all his ways, and to cleave unto him; then the Lord would drive out nations greater and mightier than Israel. Heaven was never about everybody being equal and holding hands; heaven is Israel gaining possession and power over the nations, and that has always been the gospel.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
This is the same word the Lord foretold to Moses that Joshua now fulfills. Moses told Israel the promised land was meant to be “as the days of heaven upon the earth.” The condition was “if ye shall diligently keep all these commandments which I command you, to do them, to love the Lord your God, to walk in all his ways, and to cleave unto him; Then will the Lord drive out all these nations from before you, and ye shall possess greater nations and mightier than yourselves.”

Then the very promise repeated to Joshua: “Every place whereon the soles of your feet shall tread shall be yours: from the wilderness and Lebanon, from the river, the river Euphrates, even unto the uttermost sea shall your coast be. There shall no man be able to stand before you: for the Lord your God shall lay the fear of you and the dread of you upon all the land that ye shall tread upon, as he hath said unto you.”

Heaven was never about everybody being equal and holding hands; heaven is Israel gaining possession and power over the nations, and that has always been the gospel. The proof that we have not kept the commandments is that we own nothing today. Even land bought and paid for is not truly yours: fail to pay the real estate tax and it is taken by eminent domain and sold at auction. It was never meant to be that way; Israel was supposed to have ownership of the earth.
